rows.summary: AWS Site-to-Site VPN now supports modifying tunnel bandwidth between standard (up to 1.25 Gbps) and large (up to 5 Gbps) on existing connections, making it easier to update your VPN connections’ bandwidth per your organization’s need. ...

rows.title: AWS Site-to-Site VPN now supports BGP logging for VPN tunnels
rows.summary: AWS Site-to-Site VPN now allows customers to publish Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) logs from VPN tunnels to AWS CloudWatch, providing enhanced visibility into VPN configurations and simplifying troubleshooting of connectivity issues. ...

rows.title: AWS Site-to-Site VPN is collaborating with eero to simplify remote connectivity
rows.summary: AWS Site-to-Site VPN is collaborating with eero to simplify how customers connect their remote sites to AWS. This collaboration will help customers to establish secure connectivity between their remote sites and AWS in just a few clicks. Many AWS customers operate hundreds of remote sites - from restaurants and retail stores to gas stations and mobile offices. ...

rows.title: AWS Site-to-Site VPN announces VPN Concentrator
rows.summary: AWS Site-to-Site VPN launches VPN Concentrator, a new feature that simplifies multi-site connectivity for distributed enterprises. VPN Concentrator is suitable for customers who need to connect 25+ remote sites to AWS, with each site needing low bandwidth (under 100 Mbps). ...

rows.title: Site-to-Site VPN Concentrators
rows.summary: Site-to-Site VPN Concentrators provide a centralized hub for managing multiple VPN connections with enhanced scalability and simplified network architecture.
rows.quote: | [Site-to-Site VPN Concentrators](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-concentrator.html) | Site-to-Site VPN Concentrators provide a centralized hub for managing multiple VPN connections with enhanced scalability and simplified network architecture. | November 15, 2025 |

rows.title: AWS Site-to-Site VPN announces 5 Gbps bandwidth tunnels
rows.summary: AWS Site-to-Site VPN now supports VPN connections with up to 5 Gbps bandwidth per tunnel, a 4x improvement from existing limit of 1.25 Gbps. This increased bandwidth benefits customers who require high-capacity connections for bandwidth-intensive hybrid applications, big data migrations, and disaster recovery architectures while maintaining traffic encryption between AWS and their remote sites. ...

rows.title: Site-to-Site VPN support for Large Bandwidth Tunnels
rows.summary: Site-to-Site VPN now supports Large Tunnel Bandwidth, enabling transit gateway and Cloud WAN VPN attachments with up to 5 Gbps throughput.
rows.quote: | [Site-to-Site VPN support for Large Bandwidth Tunnels](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/large-bandwidth-tunnels.html) | Site-to-Site VPN now supports Large Tunnel Bandwidth, enabling transit gateway and Cloud WAN VPN attachments with up to 5 Gbps throughput. | September 25, 2025 |

rows.title: IPv6 support for AWS Site-to-Site VPN for outer tunnel IPs
rows.summary: Site-to-Site VPN now supports IPv6 addresses for the outer tunnel IPs on Transit Gateway and Cloud WAN VPN connections. This enables full IPv6 migration with IPv6 addresses for both outer tunnel IPs and inner packet IPs (IPv6-in-IPv6), as well as IPv6 outer tunnel IPs with IPv4 inner packet IPs (IPv4-in-IPv6).
rows.quote: | [IPv6 support for AWS Site-to-Site VPN for outer tunnel IPs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/ipv4-ipv6.html) | Site-to-Site VPN now supports IPv6 addresses for the outer tunnel IPs on Transit Gateway and Cloud WAN VPN connections. This enables full IPv6 migration with IPv6 addresses for both outer tunnel IPs and inner packet IPs (IPv6-in-IPv6), as well as IPv6 outer tunnel IPs with IPv4 inner packet IPs (IPv4-in-IPv6). | July 1, 2025 |
